## 1. Verdict in 5 lines

1. **The PR is a real net improvement.** It closes several P0 issues that the previous audit marked as open: handshake 0xFA, timeouts for `runAngle`/`runDistance`/color sensor, Lock in camera, autorestart systemd, global recovery in Python. **This needs to be protected, not broken.**
2. **The fear of "dead fixes" is UNFOUNDED.** The flags system does NOT turn off anything (see §3). The resilience safety net is **ALIVE** in the firmware being flashed.
3. **BUT there are real NEW bugs** in the evacuation/rescue code (1 P0 + several P1) that no one had seen because that code is new.
4. **Two security gaps were left open either intentionally or by oversight:** no RX failsafe on the Teensy (P0) and flag #63 turned off desynchronizes the serial after each maneuver (P1).
5. **No change has a documented bench run** (golden rule #3 not fulfilled), and the new evacuation — which is half of the useful score — is the least tested.

## 3. Status of fixes in the new code

### ⭐ MOST IMPORTANT: the flags system does NOT kill the fixes

This was the biggest fear and is now **resolved in favor**. In `priority_fix_flags.h:5` the master `kEnableAllPriorityFixes = false`, but in `main.cpp:120-178` **each helper uses OR, not AND**:

```cpp
bool fixIssue60Enabled() {
    return kEnableAllPriorityFixes || kFixIssue60RunDistanceTimeout;  // OR
}
```

With the master set to `false`, the `||` short-circuits the **individual flag**. Since the individual flags are set to `true` (#57/#58/#59/#60/#61/#62/#67/#74/#75/#76/#112), **the fixes ARE ACTIVE**. The master is not a kill-switch: it is an override "force-all-on." **The safety net exists in the binary going to Incheon.** The only one turned off: **#63** (`KeepSerialDuringMotions`, master false + individual false → dead, see §4 bug N-08).

> ⚠️ **Future semantic trap:** the naming is misleading. If someone sets the master to `false` expecting "safe mode without fixes," they are mistaken (the fixes remain). And setting it to `true` means you can **no longer** turn off an individual fix. It should be called `kForceEnableAllFixes`. **Do not touch the master.** To turn off a fix that proves counterproductive in the bench, lower its individual flag.

| **I-02** | **Orphan flags and variables that mislead.** `fixIssue57Enabled()` defined, **0 call sites** (the team thinks #57 is "applied by the flag" and the flag controls nothing). `#67` applies **without** gate (`drivebase.cpp:17`) → the flag is decorative. `evacuacion_straight` (decl 106, only resets) and `alineado` (101, only `=false`) are zombies. `lastTurn`/`turnCooldown=600` (52-53) declared, **never used** (anti-bounce of green halfway). | `main.cpp:120-124, 101, 106, 52-53` |
| **I-03** | **`veces_deposit` and `ball_counter` initialize at 2** (the "finished" value), not at 0. It works because they reset upon entering rescue (1597-1598), but **the switch-off reset (1407-1418) does NOT touch them.** If the operator turns off/restarts the switch **during** rescue (common in competition), they remain at arbitrary value → deposit/output with corrupt count. | `main.cpp:103-104, 1407-1418, 1597-1598` |
| **I-04** | **Break of `case 12` depends on flag #58 to avoid falling through to `case 14`** (180 turn). Control flow of a `switch` coupled to a feature flag = anti-pattern. Harmless today **only** because `green_state==14` never reaches from the RPi (unreachable code). **Fix:** unconditional `break`, leave the flag only for the timeout. | `main.cpp:1740-1744` |
| **I-05** | **`case 12` / `green_state 14-17` is unreachable code.** The RPi in line only emits `green_state ∈ {0,1,2,3,10,11}` (verified `Main.py:790-874`). The `case 12` (50+ lines with its timeout #58) **never runs in competition.** The #58 protects dead code. **Fix:** confirm with Lucio that it was an abandoned feature and delete. | `main.cpp:1536-1539, 1695-1744` |
| **I-06** | **Red end line by VISION is discarded.** The RPi sends `green_state=10` (simple) / `11` (double), but the firmware in line routine **never reads 10/11** (the switch only handles 0/1/2/3/14). It only cuts if the physical APDS classifies 'Red' (`color_detected=="Red"`, 1504). Information that the RPi already calculates is thrown away. See O-end-line. | `main.cpp:1504-1508` vs `Main.py:871-874` |
| **I-07** | **Three implementations of color classification in the live firmware:** `get_color_fast`/`update_color_nonblocking` (the one used), `get_color_old` (676) and `get_color_blocking_legacy` (731), the last two **0 call sites**. Moreover, the thresholds for 'Red' **differ between the `print` and the `return`** in the legacy. Confuses the maintenance of calibration. | `main.cpp:676-729, 731-802` |
| **I-08** | **Double trigger for entry to rescue with different criteria:** vision (`Main.py:838` silver_mask BGR + area>50 → `silver_line=1`) and Teensy color sensor (`main.cpp:1494` `get_color_fast=='Silver'`). Coexist without a clear source of truth. If one gives a false positive, entry to the area is erratic. | `Main.py:838` vs `main.cpp:1494` |
| **I-09** | **Doc duplicated in the same PR that says to deduplicate.** `variables_doc.md` was emptied marking "Deprecated TDP Copy" pointing to `../../../TDP.md`, but the PR adds `TDP.md` at the root **AND** `docs/tdp/TDP-IITA-2026.md` (same content, 458 lines each). Violates "one single source of truth" in the same PR. | `TDP.md` and `docs/tdp/TDP-IITA-2026.md` |
| **I-10** | **Outdated range contract.** The comment says `green_state: 0..20` (`Main.py:22-23`) but the code uses up to 11. Verify that `SERIAL_MAX_GREEN_STATE` (#74) is ≥ the actual values or valid green_states will be rejected — and `serialPayloadOutOfRange` does `continue` **without** resetting `serial5state`, desynchronizing the next frame. `cut_line` (778,781) is calculated and never used. | `Main.py:22, 778` vs `main.cpp:881` |

## 6. Competitive improvement opportunities (champion's eye)

> Prioritized by impact on SCORE. The 2026 scoring multiplies the entire field by **×1.4 for each live victim evacuated**. A robot that finishes the line but fails the evacuation leaves more points on the table than any speed optimization.

### 🎯 LEVERAGE #1 — Secure the EVACUATION (maximum leverage)

It is half of the useful score and today is the most fragile. Three chained holes that no champion would accept:
- **(a) Room coverage at the mercy of chance.** `avance_recto()`, `lado_pared()`, `pelotita()`, `esquinas_negro[]` are **defined but DEAD** (0 call sites). The robot only reacts to what the camera sees, **without systematic sweeping of the perimeter or memory of what victims it has already collected.** Ball in corner out of frame = never collected.
- **(b) Fixed 180° deposit** (`main.cpp:1830,1850`) that assumes the area is always in front. In asymmetric areas (the judges set it up this way) **deposits in the air.**
- **(c) Final exit not robustly implemented** (N-21).

**Realistic leverage in 10 days — NOT redesign, but YES:** (1) wire `avance_recto()` as search mode when the camera does not see a ball — **requires fixing B4 first** (`leer_yaw` does not assign the global yaw); (2) do **20 timed evacuation runs** measuring capture rate and correct area deposit, and tune timings **with data, not by eye**. *Impact: HIGH. A run of ~30 pts of line becomes 30×1.4×1.4≈59 pts.* → **Laureano + Lucio.**

### 🎯 LEVERAGE #2 — Robust color calibration for Incheon light (consistency)

What kills runs in a new stadium is not the strategy, it is that the calibrated thresholds in **Salta** do not match the light of **Songdo**. Three color systems with hardcoded thresholds that will desynchronize: (a) `Main.py` fixed BGR/LAB/HSV (71-80) + **silver_mask in BGR with HSV thresholds (B2)**; (b) APDS9960 on Teensy with `known_colors[]` and magic thresholds (`c>1700`, `R/C>0.240`); (c) `CLASS_THRESH` of YOLO.

**Action in 10 days:** (1) **fix camera exposure and white balance** — today the auto-exposure "pumps" when bright silver/white enters and ruins the masks (the `anti_flash` attacks the symptom; the cause is the auto-exposure). It is ~2 lines of `cv2.CAP_PROP`; (2) write a **recalibration checklist for the pit** (10-20s before each round); (3) load thresholds from editable JSON without recompiling. *Impact: HIGH for CONSISTENCY — reducing variance between runs is worth more than raising the maximum.* → **Lucio + Benjamin.**

### 🎯 LEVERAGE #3 — Turn the already written novelty into measured evidence for the TDP

The TDP weighs **12% of the total** and the 2026 rubric added "Reliability Tests & QA". The team ALREADY has the strongest novelty asset **written and running**: the **anti-flash** pipeline (direct response to rule 3.9 of flashing LEDs) and the **multimodal victim validation design** (vision+conductivity+reflectance, rule 3.10). No reference team (Overengineering², Airborne, Danesh) documents this because they competed under 2024/2025 rules. **It is the uncopyable narrative.** But today it is "we designed," not "we measured": the TEST_LOG is almost empty and **conductivity is NOT embedded** (pin 26 is not read).

**High ROI in 10 days:** (1) **implement conductivity** — ~15 lines + 1 pin + 2 wires (already documented) → turns the claim into a real feature that rejects false victims (rule 3.10); (2) record 15-20 frames with flash (a flashlight), run detection with/without `anti_flash`, put the table in TEST_LOG → N1 goes from "we designed" to "we designed and validated" (the difference between 3 and 6 in the rubric). **Credibility care:** present ONLY what is embedded as "the robot does"; the rest as "in integration." A world judge dismantles inflated claims. → **Benjamin + Lucio.**

### Other opportunities (order of impact)

- **O-1 — Tune a real Kp in the PID** (today `kp=0/ki=22`, pure integral). A small Kp gives immediate response to error and improves wheel-to-wheel consistency and corner tracing. *Medium risk (re-test of the 4 wheels). Only if done BEFORE June 15 or do not touch.* → **Laureano.**
- **O-2 — Proportional speed scheduling on line** instead of two speeds 25/55 (B5): progressive braking when entering a curve, minimum at the apex. Less overshoot (going off the line) + more speed on straight. → **Laureano.**
- **O-3 — Recover lost line** (line-search): upon losing black, today the RPi sends `angle=0` and the robot continues straight blindly. A ±sweep with the IMU searching for black saves tiles in gaps. *Requires fixed B4.* → **Laureano + Lucio.**
- **O-evasion — Evasion by sensor instead of `random()`** (N-16): the robot ALREADY reads `left/right_distance`. Minimum: `lado = (left_distance > right_distance) ? left : right`. The blind random fails ~50% when the space is on the other side. → **Laureano.**
- **O-end-line — Close end of line by vision** (I-06): leverage `green_state 10/11` that the RPi already sends, redundant with the APDS. Reliable stop on the red end line. → **Laureano + Lucio.**
- **O-resilience — Bidirectional failsafe + hardware WDT.** Turn the 0xFA into a periodic heartbeat (every ~200ms both sides) closes N-01 **and** the inverse case (Teensy hung). Build the **WDT_T4** of the Teensy with `feed()` in loop + long whiles: catches ALL hangs, even unanticipated ones (case 1, N-14). *Standard practice for top teams, low cost.* → **Laureano** (+ Lucio for the RPi side).
- **O-budget — Cut oversized clamp delays.** Each ball chains ~8 `nonBlockingDelay` of 1000-1400ms ≈ **9-10s/ball ×3 ≈ 30s** still. **Time the complete run**; if it does not reach for 3 balls + 2 deposits + exit, cut delays (several 1000ms can be 600-700ms if the servo has already arrived) and **prioritize the 2 live ones** (worth the multiplier) over the dead one. *Golden rule: evacuate 2 live > attempt 3 and run out of time.* → **Laureano + Benjamin (bench with stopwatch).**

## 8. Coach's closing — the 3 things of greatest impact in 25 days

Team: this PR is a real leap from the robot we audited in May. They closed P0 of resilience, the handshake, the timeouts, the camera threading. **That is already won — do not break it in haste.** Use the individual flags as a net: if a new fix breaks something in Incheon, turn off **its** flag, do not revert code.

Now, where do we place the chips in these 25 days, in order:

1. **CLOSE THE TWO P0 THIS WEEK.** The robot that goes off the table when the RPi hangs (**N-01**) and the autostart that cannot find its own file (**N-02**) are the difference between competing and watching. They are low risk and can be tested in the bench in an afternoon. Do not reach the freeze without this.

2. **SECURE THE EVACUATION — it is half the score.** The ×1.4 multiplier for live victim is worth more than any speed optimization. Do not redesign: fix **B4** (yaw), wire a minimum sweep (**LEVERAGE #1**), fix the re-triggering of deposits (**N-04/N-05**), and do **20 timed runs** tuning with data. Today the evacuation is at the mercy of chance and is the least tested.

3. **CONSISTENCY > MAXIMUM: in-situ color calibration + measure for the TDP.** What kills robots in a world championship is that they work at home and fail on the field due to the light. **Fix exposure/WB** (2 lines, root cause of pumping) and arrive with a **recalibration checklist for the pit**. And in passing, **embed conductivity** and record flash tests: they turn the strongest novelty narrative you have (12% of the TDP) from "we designed" to "we measure."

**Final discipline:** everything touched goes to bench and to `TEST_LOG.md` before merging (golden rule #3). Split PR #129 into code and docs to merge the safe code NOW. And do not touch the PID or the master flag unless you have a bench run that justifies it.

To gain experience in Incheon — and to arrive with the robot **consistent**, which is what separates the podium.

— The coach
